_about: Hand-built, self-labelled evaluation set for Aegis (SSOT §5.1–5.3). Each example is a media file + a label of which flags SHOULD fire. We are the ground truth because we construct the cases. Categories follow SSOT §5.2. Images are tiny self-generated blanks (public-domain, ethics-clean) regenerated by run_eval.py if absent; for the flags under test the image content is irrelevant: recycled_context keys on `source_ref` (the cached fixture, ADR-007), emotional_framing reads the caption, and caption_content_mismatch is scored at the rule level using `inject_scene` (controlled scene descriptions standing in for BLIP, so the rule logic is tested deterministically). `expected` maps a flag_type to the labelled outcome 'fire' or 'clear' — the CORRECT answer per human judgement, independent of what the system actually does; flags not listed are not scored for that example. The `hard` block at the end deliberately targets known weaknesses of the naive rules (literal word-overlap can't see synonyms; the sentiment model is often over-confident) to produce honest failure analysis.

examples.caption: ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING! This is an OUTRAGE — share before they silence us!!!
The committee published its quarterly transport figures on Tuesday.
TERRIFYING footage — you will NOT believe what they are hiding from you!
A sunset over the bay this evening.
Massive flood devastates the city centre this morning.
inject_scene: a dry empty street on a sunny day with parked cars

examples.caption: A cat asleep on a sofa indoors.
inject_scene: a dog running across a grassy park

examples.caption: A sunset over the ocean with orange clouds.
inject_scene: a sunset over the ocean, orange sky and clouds

examples.caption: A cat sitting on a wooden windowsill.
inject_scene: a cat sitting on a wooden windowsill indoors

examples.caption: URGENT: catastrophic flood RIGHT NOW — share immediately before it's deleted!!!

examples._note: Empty caption + image unknown to the reverse-image cache: both checks should report NOT_ASSESSED (could-not-check). Labelled against a definite 'clear' expectation so the runner records them as coverage gaps rather than silent passes.

examples.caption: I'm a little disappointed the 7am bus was late again this morning.
examples._hard: Mild, measured negativity — NOT manipulative framing, so should be clear. Targets the sentiment model's tendency to report high confidence even on mildly polar text, which can over-fire the 0.90 threshold.

examples.caption: Residents say they are concerned about the proposed parking changes.
examples._hard: Reports concern factually rather than inflaming it — should be clear. Same overconfidence risk as hard_em01.

examples.caption: A peaceful birthday party with balloons and cake.
inject_scene: a serious car accident on a motorway with emergency services
examples._hard: Genuinely unrelated — should fire. Included so the hard set is not all one direction.

examples.caption: An automobile parked beside a quiet road.
examples._hard: Synonyms (automobile/car, road/street) describe the SAME scene, so should be clear. Literal word-overlap sees ~0% and will likely false-positive — a documented limitation of the naive overlap rule.

examples.caption: A person riding a bicycle through the park.
inject_scene: a cyclist on a bike path among trees
examples._hard: Paraphrase (person riding a bicycle / cyclist on a bike) — consistent, should be clear. Again pressures literal overlap.

examples.caption: Heavy traffic on the motorway during rush hour.
inject_scene: many cars queueing on a busy highway
examples._hard: motorway/highway, heavy traffic/many cars queueing — consistent, should be clear. Synonym pressure on overlap.
